summary: The oldest lighthouse on Canada's west coast, first lit in 1860 at the mouth of Esquimalt Harbour, gutted by fire in 1957 and now a Parks Canada site.

access.note: Parks Canada site with grounds open daily; lighthouse open weekends Oct 16-Apr 30 and daily May 1-Oct 15; check notices.

notes_for_editor: Many facts rest on LighthouseFriends (itself citing Graham 1985 and Gibbs 1986) and Parks Canada's web page; Lambeth and Jeune 1980 (Parks Canada MS Report 356) is the standard history but could not be read. Sources conflict on Davies's pay and voyage, designer, tower height, designation year (1958 vs 1960), automation (1928 vs 1929), and how long the Bevis women ran the light. Gosse (13 Oct 1909, $360, p.268) and Johnston (30 Jul 1901, p.70) were checked against the page images. The John Davies of Parks Canada's 1898 list is not linked to the John Davies at Fiddle Reef in the 1902 report. Newspapers search not applicable (Canadian).
